Here are the complete R code solutions for all tasks across Parts A through E.

Part A: Basic Operations
A1
v <- seq(5, 50, by = 5)
v

cat("Length:", length(v), "\n")
cat("Sum:", sum(v), "\n")
cat("Mean:", mean(v), "\n")
A2
w <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), times = 4)
z <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), each = 4)

w
z
A3
# Remainder of 17 divided by 5
17 %% 5

# Integer division of 17 by 5
17 %/% 5

# 2 to the power of 10
2^10

# Square root of 144
sqrt(144)

# Pi rounded to 3 decimals
round(pi, 3)
A4
a <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)
b <- c(1, 3, 5, 7)

# a + b
a + b

# a * b
a * b

# Logical comparison a > b
a > b

# Dot product sum(a * b)
sum(a * b)
A5
paste("Student", 1:3, sep = "-")

# Datatypes:
class(42)     # "numeric"

class(411)    # "numeric"

Part B: Data Frames and Conditional Statements
B1
students <- data.frame(
  id = 1:8,
  name = c("Alice", "Bruno", "Chen", "Dana", "Elif", "Farid", "Grace", "Hiro"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M"),
  section = c("A", "B", "A", "C", "B", "C", "A", "B"),
  midterm = c(78, 85, 92, 67, 74, 88, 95, 59),
  final = c(82, 79, 96, 71, 80, 91, 93, 65),
  attendance = c(95, 88, 100, 72, 90, 85, 98, 60),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

students
B2
str(students)
dim(students)
colnames(students)
summary(students)
B3
students$average <- round(rowMeans(students[, c("midterm", "final")]), 1)
students
B4
students$passed <- students$average >= 70 & students$attendance >= 75
students
B5
students$standing <- ifelse(students$average >= 90, "Honors",
                     ifelse(students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))
students
B6
classify <- function(score) {
  if (score >= 85) {
    return("Distinction")
  } else if (score >= 70) {
    return("Merit")
  } else if (score >= 50) {
    return("Pass")
  } else {
    return("Fail")
  }
}

# Test with vector
test_scores <- c(90, 73, 55, 40)
sapply(test_scores, classify)
Part C: rbind() and cbind()
C1
new_students <- data.frame(
  id = c(9, 10),
  name = c("Ines", "Jamal"),
  sex = c("F", "M"),
  section = c("C", "A"),
  midterm = c(81, 70),
  final = c(84, 68),
  attendance = c(92, 80),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Compute derived columns matching the original logic
new_students$average <- round(rowMeans(new_students[, c("midterm", "final")]), 1)
new_students$passed <- new_students$average >= 70 & new_students$attendance >= 75
new_students$standing <- ifelse(new_students$average >= 90, "Honors",
                         ifelse(new_students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))

# Append rows
students_all <- rbind(students, new_students)
students_all
C2
quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6)

students_all <- cbind(students_all, quiz = quiz)
students_all
class(students_all)
C3
m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final)

# Append mean row
m <- rbind(m, mean = colMeans(m))
m
C4
# Explanation:
# rbinding data frames with mismatched column names raises an error because R 
# requires identical column names and structures to align rows correctly. 
# Wrapping the operation in tryCatch safely captures this condition and handles 
# the execution without crashing the script.

bad <- data.frame(wrong_name = 1, wrong_score = 2)

tryCatch(
  rbind(students, bad), 
  error = function(e) {
    message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  }
)
Part D: Subsetting
D1
# Method 1: $
students_all$name

# Method 2: [["name"]]
students_all[["name"]]

# Method 3: [, "name"]
students_all[, "name"]
D2
students_all[2:5, c("name", "midterm", "final")]
D3
students_all[students_all$attendance > 90, ]
D4
subset(
  students_all, 
  sex == "F" & (section == "A" | section == "C") & final >= 75,
  select = c("name", "section", "final")
)
D5
# Highest average
highest_idx <- which.max(students_all$average)
cat("Highest average student:", students_all$name[highest_idx], "\n")

# Lowest average
lowest_idx <- which.min(students_all$average)
cat("Lowest average student:", students_all$name[lowest_idx], "\n")
D6
sorted_students <- students_all[order(-students_all$average), ]
head(sorted_students, 3)
Part E: Basic Factors
E1
students_all$section <- factor(students_all$section)
students_all$sex <- factor(students_all$sex)

levels(students_all$section)
levels(students_all$sex)
E2
# Output of the two-way table shows a contingency frequency count cross-tabulating counts per sex across each section.
table(students_all$sex, students_all$section)
E3
as.integer(students_all$sex)

# Explanation:
# The integers represent the underlying numerical codes assigned to factor levels 
# in alphabetical order (1 corresponds to "F", 2 corresponds to "M").
E4
sex_label <- factor(students_all$sex, levels = c("F", "M"), labels = c("Female", "Male"))
students_all$sex_label <- sex_label

levels(students_all$sex_label)
E5
summary(students_all$sex_label)

# Mean average grade per sex level
mean(students_all$average[students_all$sex_label == "Female"])
mean(students_all$average[students_all$sex_label == "Male"])
